question.text: An open elevator ascends vertically with an instantaneous speed of 10 m/s while accelerating upward at a rate of 2 m/s². At this moment, a ball is thrown straight up with a speed of 20 m/s relative to the ground from the base of the elevator. Taking g = 10 m/s², calculate the following:

parts.label: a
parts.asks: The time elapsed before the ball returns to the elevator floor.

parts.label: b
parts.asks: The vertical displacement of both the elevator and the ball at that moment.

parts.label: c
parts.asks: The total distance covered by the ball during this duration.

conditions: initial upward velocity of lift = 10 m/s
constant upward acceleration of lift = 2 m/s²
initial upward velocity of ball relative to ground = 20 m/s
ball starts from lift floor at t = 0
acceleration due to gravity g = 10 m/s² downward

solution.approach: Write the displacement of the lift and of the ball as functions of time from the same starting point, and set them equal to find when they meet again.

steps.text: Write the lift's displacement, starting with an upward speed of 10 m/s and an upward acceleration of 2 m/s².
Write the ball's displacement, projected upward at 20 m/s and acted on only by gravity.
Set the two displacements equal and solve for t, keeping the positive, nonzero root.
Substitute t = 5/3 s into either displacement equation to get the common displacement at that instant.

Check the ball's velocity at this instant to see if it has already turned back; since it is still positive, the ball has travelled straight up the whole time, so the distance travelled equals its displacement.

final_answer.value: (a) t = 5/3 s ≈ 1.67 s, (b) both lift and ball at 175/9 m ≈ 19.4 m, (c) distance travelled by ball ≈ 19.4 m

common_mistakes.text: Taking t = 0 as the meeting time instead of discarding it as the starting instant, since both objects begin together at t = 0.
Assuming the ball has already reached its highest point by t = 5/3 s and using its full rise time of 2 s to compute distance, when it is in fact still rising.
